name: Designing New Molecules
title: Designing New Molecules
answer: Designing new molecules with AI covers computational generation and evaluation of candidate drug molecules, including small molecules, peptides, and antibodies. It spans de novo design, property prediction, and molecular simulation to find compounds with desired activity, selectivity, and safety profiles. The work sits within drug discovery and molecular simulation, where AI models propose structures that medicinal chemists then prioritize for synthesis and testing. This page focuses on the design stage rather than clinical use or patient care.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on GPU clusters and cloud compute for training generative models and running physics-based simulations. Data infrastructure includes large libraries of known compounds, protein structures, and assay results, often stored in specialized databases. Models are typically served through internal platforms that connect generation, scoring, and visualization tools. Many teams use containerized pipelines to move candidate molecules from generation to docking and molecular dynamics.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Generative models such as variational autoencoders, diffusion models, and reinforcement learning agents propose new molecular structures. Each candidate is scored by property predictors for binding affinity, solubility, metabolic stability, and toxicity. Physics-based methods like docking and molecular dynamics refine or validate the most promising designs. Active learning loops feed experimental results back into the model to improve the next round of proposals.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on who owns AI generated molecules, how training data was licensed, and whether a model reproduces patented structures. Safety and efficacy claims require experimental validation, and regulators expect clear provenance for how a candidate was designed and tested. Product liability for AI designed drugs is still unsettled, and this site tracks active lawsuits against AI companies in the medical space. Teams should document model versions, training data, and human review steps for each candidate.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The field is moving toward tighter integration of generative design, simulation, and automated synthesis to shorten discovery cycles. Models are likely to handle more multi objective optimization, balancing potency, selectivity, and pharmacokinetics earlier. As experimental feedback loops grow, design systems may become more reliable at proposing synthesizable and developable molecules. The main open question is whether these tools can consistently produce candidates that succeed in clinical trials, not just in computational benchmarks.
